followRulesDisabledNote: 18/10/2026 (BTN-1, probe v10, /contact/ and its de and ru copies): Contact Form 7's Send request is held disabled until the consent box is ticked. The template draws it in its orange at 60% opacity (tracy-base sections-extra.css), the call to action still read as one; sections.css hands the disabled face to the system's disabled roles, and with the opacity on top it stood as a pale grey slab on its card (Moxie #777568 on #d5d1b9, 1.6:1 off the card): no visitor would read it as the form's button. Under a system it keeps the system's accent and its words, the template's opacity still saying it is not yet pressable. This rule stays in the contract (dot 3, 19/10/2026): it is a worn-only interaction the theme cannot draw itself. The theme keeps reading the disabled roles (sections.css, var(--ds-c-disabled-bg, accent)), which every disabled control should; with no worn marker on a WordPress page it cannot drop its 60% opacity only while a system is worn. Measured without this rule on 1.3.8 (/contact/, Moxie and Figma, light and dark, probe v10): BTN-1 lostButtons on every run (Moxie light #d5d1b9 on the card #eae5cc, dark #2a2a24 on #1a1a1a, under 1.25:1); with it, none.
followRulesNote: 15/10/2026 (every declared page measured): the theme and the demo content paint words on the brand ink with the accent-on preset (white in the template, its own white on the ink); under a system the ink takes the system's ink role (templateVars) while accent-on is the system's word on its accent (Moxie's black), so the team names, the ink chips, the priced list's titles and the content's inline ink blocks (the projects chips, the investor table head, the careers quote, the slide numbers) read 1:1. Words on the ink take the ink's own words (on-ink); an inline colour is beaten with !important, as only that outranks a style attribute
